steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Oh! What happened...?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Are you okay, Bibeak?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Gee, Bibeak, you're so excited to go home you can't even hold your cup?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Well, as they say in Yan: Break a cup, break a trouble. Sounds like everything's gonna be great!

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Don't worry about it. This is your send-off party. You sit right there, and I'll go get you a new cup.

spans.text: Don't worry about it. This is
send-off party. You sit right there, and I'll go get you a new cup.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Ah, watch out! Lemme clean this up first.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Bibeak...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: What's the matter?

a.text: We're both doing fine. No need to worry about us.
I've been keeping your room just the way you left it. Your dad has new glasses now. I guess he should've listened when you told him to take better care of his eyes!
We're happy to hear that you've been doing well on Rhodes Island, and are really proud of the work you're doing there.

There's something we've been hesitating to tell you, but decided in the end that it's better for you to know. The culprit who infected you with Oripathy has been caught, and he's now serving a prison sentence.
I hope this helps give you some closure, after all these years. Wishing you the best over at Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (...He's been jailed for a year now, and Mom and Dad didn't tell me until now.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (They didn't need to worry. I... I don't care anymore. Yeah.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (There's a photo of Mom and... my goodness, why are Dad's new glasses that color?)

spans.text: (There's a photo of Mom and... my goodness, why are Dad's new glasses

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Mom definitely picked it on purpose.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Are these clothes for me? And a new rapier... It looks nice and handles well. Must be Dad's work.)

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Looks like your folks sent you enough stuff to fill a small house.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: And I suppose you'll be using this sword in training later?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Yeah, Dad designed it for me.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: That's so sweet. I bet you were very close back home.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: N-No, not really...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Ooh, getting embarrassed?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: ...Keep that up and you're not getting that new skirt you wanted.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Ouch, now that's below the belt! What would I even wear without you making clothes for me?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Come on, stop teasing me.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Haha. Alright, I'll let you read your mail in peace.
Bibeak casts her gaze towards the other letter on the table.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: The sender's name isn't written, only the address: 'Municipal Prison.'
'Kind lady, I write this letter with gratitude in my heart. I feel that I have found peace in my soul, and would like to share this joy with you.'
'Plagued by guilt over harming an innocent soul with Originium, I sought help from a psychiatrist, who helped me deal with my issues.'
'He said that everyone should have the chance to forgive themselves for their mistakes. I gave myself such a chance, forgave my own mistake, and now I feel at peace.'
'I asked him how you might be feeling now. I believe you need to break free of the cycle of hatred and pain in order to find peace.'
'Please hear me out, kind lady. We must forgive ourselves and forgive others, put down our hatred, and even embrace our enemies, in order to move on to a new life.'

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Why are you staring into space? Who was that letter from?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's him... the man who...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Who? Oh... what did he say?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: He said he found forgiveness and peace.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: That's... a good thing. Right?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I've been so busy these past few years that I'd almost completely forgotten about it. I don't really think about it anymore.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: The man said he... I don't know which psychiatrist he talked to, but he said he found peace in his heart, and no longer feels pain from hurting me.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'm thinking... I've almost forgotten about it. He's in prison, but he let things go too, in his own way.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: So once he's released, he should be able to start a new life, shouldn't he?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Hehe... that's good. Time to close the book on this. I...
A tear flows down the corner of Bibeak's eye.
Tears begin to flow uncontrollably, as though a dam had burst inside her eyes.
She feels as anxious as she is confused.
She tries to wipe her tears with her hand, but the gesture is futile as even more take their place. She begins to cry uncontrollably.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Bibeak?! What's going on? Are you okay?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: W-What's happened to me?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Come on, here's a handkerchief!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I... I don't know what's wrong with me...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I must be overcome with joy about getting to visit home...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: S-Sorry...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: It's okay, it's okay. Go wash your face. I'll get you a cup of warm water.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Come on, go!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: O-Okay!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: What happened to me?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Did you ask, Bibeak?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Yes, I'll be getting off when Rhodes Island stops to resupply in Columbia next month. Amiya gave me two months off.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'll be spending that time with my parents, maybe going on a trip with them. But I'm thinking about what to bring them.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Souvenirs from other countries? Perhaps something from Rhodes Island? Or something I made myself?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Should I have it sent by Messenger? Or bring it in person?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Hey, don't get yourself in a twist over this. There's still plenty of time to prepare.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Whoa! Your hands are ice-cold! What's the matter?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Oh...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'm just nervous.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: After that letter last week, I've been thinking... I think I'll visit the prison, see that man.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: ...Bibeak.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: I admire you for making such a decision.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It... took me a week to make up my mind.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I just felt like I needed to go and take a look. After, it's my... my...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: It'll be okay. It's a way to come to terms with the past. You're very brave for doing it.

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Let's go. And maybe we can ask some other people about what souvenirs to bring home.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Lily? Sorry for bothering you. I'm going home next month and wanted some advice on what would make a good souvenir.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Drunk Fins from Yan? Okay... thanks. I'll think about it.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: You brought cookies you learned how to make from Gummy? That sounds fun. I'll go and ask in the kitchen. Thank you!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Oh, Gummy is out on a field mission? I see...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Your family loved the mission photos you brought back? Hm, let me think...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thanks, I think I have a better idea now.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (It seems that families prefer gifts made by the operators themselves.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Something personal, something filled with love...)
A few days later

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: The new clothes are done already? Wowie, that was fast! I'm so glad you're my sewing teacher.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I just taught you some of the basics. I wouldn't say I'm your teacher exactly.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I... only just got to the point where I'm cutting the cloth right. Who knows how long it'll take me to start making clothes for Dad?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: You're doing well for a beginner. Just keep it up, and you'll improve.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: So, after asking everyone what they took when they went home, you ended up making clothes for your parents.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Yeah, I asked people what they brought.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Their families preferred boxes of homemade cookies—even when they got crushed in transit—over Ursus honeyed mead or rare Sami smoked jerky.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I think it's because you put more of yourself in the things you make on your own.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: For example, I just realized that I didn't know my parents' sizes anymore, so I couldn't make anything too close-fitting. I ended up making them jackets.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Jackets are good. Warm and nice to look at. But you're not going back until next month, right? Do you really need to be pulling all-nighters?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I... just feel anxious when I'm not doing anything these days. I feel like I have to keep myself busy.

spans.text: I... just feel anxious when I'm not doing anything these days. I feel like I

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Probably because you're going home. Happens to everyone when they're excited.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Maybe... it's 'cause you're going to see the guy who hurt you. You sure that's a good idea?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I've always reckoned you should stay away from the bad guys.

spans.text: I've always reckoned you should stay

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I was a little concerned when I heard that too... What are you even going to say to him? What if it was a trick? What if he says something you don't want to hear?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I don't know...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It should be fine... I think?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's just a normal prison visit. There will be plenty of guards around, and we'll have a layer of glass between us.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'm not going there to do anything in particular, just to see how he's doing in prison.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Considering he wrote that letter and talked to a psychiatrist there, I guess he wants to live better too.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: If he finds peace and gets a new start on life, good for him. That's what I think. Am I wrong?

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: If I were you, I'd wear my best clothes and tell him I'm doing great. Show him that I'm not affected at all.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: But I'm not you, Bibeak. Do whatever you want.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Whatever I want...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Hey, whatcha girls up to? I heard the word 'clothes' from outside the door.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Lava's got a ton of cool outfits we could put you in! Maybe the one with the mask?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: You're going to a prison, after all. Gotta assert dominance!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Ha.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Oh, come on, this is a serious conversation.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: But Bibeak just smiled, didn't she?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thank you for trying to help.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (But... what are my own thoughts?)

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Hey, why are you back at the drawing board?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (I'm designing clothes... for the prisoner...)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (If clothes represent emotions, what clothes would I design for him?)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Dark? Warm? Broken? Comfortable? Stiff? Grotesque?)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Why would I want to make clothes for him to begin with? What do these lines, this cloth, these threads mean?)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (I don't know...)

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: She's so into it she can't hear a word we're saying...

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Bibeak?
Bibeak does not answer. She continues drawing on the sheet.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Welp, guess it's time for me to take a nap.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I'm still a little worried... I hope Bibeak's parents don't let her go alone.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: But if her visit goes without incident, then we can say that this is truly over.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Bibeak! Look, Kroos is already asleep! How long have you been working today? You should take a break.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Almost... one more length of cloth...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Just a little bit more...

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Wow, you've already started cutting?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: But didn't you already finish the clothes for your parents? What's this one for?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: This is...
Bibeak stops and gazes at the rough cut of the black jacket in front of her.
The threads are messy, the cloth prickly, the edges frayed.
She instinctively reaches for her scissors, wanting to cut it up.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: This is...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I made this while thinking about the man in prison.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: You made a jacket for him?!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Mm... what's going on?

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: ...Wow.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I'm amazed, Bibeak. Looks like you've really let it go.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: It's incredible that you're making clothes for someone who hurt you.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I'd never be able to, not in a million years.
The operator stands up and pats Bibeak on the shoulder.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: If I were you, I'd have moved, left the place and never looked back. I wouldn't go and see the one who hurt me, and I certainly wouldn't make clothes for him.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I would've hated him for the rest of my life. I'd never forgive him.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I'd always thought you were strong and brave, but I've gained a whole new level of respect for you.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: You're amazing, really.
Bibeak opened her mouth to speak, but ended up simply smiling.
She lowers the hand holding the scissors and exhales.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thanks... I don't know why I...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's nothing, Kalin. Thanks for the kind words.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's getting late. We should call it a day.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: See ya later, Bibeak!

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Hey, Kroos, do you know when she's leaving? I want to send her off.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Maybe have a little tea party before she goes.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Sounds like fun!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Bibeak's been helping me make clothes for Dad. I-If you need help setting the place up, I can do it!

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: All ready?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Careful, eh? Cup could be hot!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Snacks, check. Ribbons, check. We're just waiting for Bibeak!

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Hey, guys! I brought her!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Sorry everyone, packing took longer than expected.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Wait, my popper's stuck! Wait—
Bang!
The operators around the table pull their poppers, sending confetti flying.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: And there we go! Bibeak's send-off party!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Want some tea, Bibeak?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Have a nice trip!

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: You always work so hard, making so many beautiful clothes for everyone, and staying on top of things in missions. Have a nice trip back home!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Come on, isn't this a bit much?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'm just visiting home for a few weeks...

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Just sit back and enjoy yourself, girl. You're the guest of honor.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: We've worked together for a few years now, and you're like a sister to me.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: You may look soft and gentle on the outside, but whenever you put your mind to something, you get it done.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's all thanks to everyone's help... I couldn't have made it on my own.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Have some snacks! Fresh out of the kitchen.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: The cafeteria staff also said they wanted to give you the best send-off they could.

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: C'mon, how 'bout we give our cups a little clink? Just don't let Fang see, or I'd never hear the end of it. 'You don't toast with teacups, blah blah blah.'

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: We're about the same age, but I'm nowhere near as brave as you are. You're a completely different person from when you first came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: T-Thanks, everybody...

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: What I admire the most is how you can bring yourself to make clothes for someone who hurt you.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: I could never.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: It's not really like that. I don't even know why I did it...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Maybe this trip will let you finally close the book on it.

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Guess this is what they mean when they say 'repay a bad deed with a good one'.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: 'Repay a bad deed with a good one'...

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Have a safe trip, Bibeak!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Er, yeah, thanks.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thanks...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (They think I'm someone who repays a bad deed with a good one.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (They think that I'm a good person, a kind person.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (They like and respect me for that. They're holding a send-off party for someone like that.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (They admire how I'm making clothes for someone who hurt me.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Mom and Dad always taught me to be dignified and well-mannered. So I should be happy for who I am now.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Am I?)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Is this the Bibeak I wanted to be?)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Do I... like myself like this?)
Bibeak feels a burning sensation as she gazes upon the smiles on the everyone's faces.
Their laughter seems jarring, the lights blinding, the teacup scorching. She feels the urge to smash something.
Her hand trembles, and the cup falls to the ground, startling her with the noise.
No one saw clearly what had happened, only its aftermath, with broken pieces and tea spilled all over the ground.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Oh! What happened...?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Are you okay, Bibeak?

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Gee, Bibeak, you're so excited to go home you can't even hold your cup?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (It's not that...)

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Well, as they say in Yan: Break a cup, break a trouble. Sounds like everything's gonna be great!

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Don't worry about it. This is your send-off party. You sit right there, and I'll go get you a new cup.

spans.text: Don't worry about it. This is
send-off party. You sit right there, and I'll go get you a new cup.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Ah, watch out! Lemme clean this up first.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Did I... just catch a glimpse of my true feelings?)

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Bibeak...

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: What's the matter?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I-It's nothing. I just lost my grip.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Let's keep going. I didn't spill anything on anyone, did I?

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'll clean it up. I see some broken pieces by my feet, and I have the best view of it.

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Huh? You sure?

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: Well, I'm just glad you're okay. That spooked me there.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I just lost my grip. It's fine.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (Now I understand. I don't like myself like this.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I... I really appreciate you all for holding this send-off for me. Some of you I've fought alongside, and some of you I've made clothes with.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: These past few years have been the best of my life.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (I really appreciate all of you, and your sincere best-wishes.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: I'll tell my parents how great the friends I've made here are, such warm and kind people who held a going away party for me.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: (I've... made my decision. This time, I won't regret it.)

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Well, the ship hasn't stopped yet. Shall we continue?

steps.name: Orchid
steps.text: Have a safe trip! Enjoy yourself!

steps.name: Kroos
steps.text: Bon voyage!

steps.name: Pinecone
steps.text: I packed you these snacks, in case you get hungry on the way!

steps.name: Idle Operator
steps.text: Stay safe!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thank you, everyone! Bye!

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Yes, I made an application and was approved for a visit from 1500 to 1530 hours.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: May I see the confirmation letter?

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: Looks like everything is in order. Follow me, please.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: There's just a little more paperwork to do.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: While we wait for the confirmation letter to be verified, I'll need you to read and acknowledge the prison visitation rules.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: I'll also need you to fill in your legal name and information on this visitor's form.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: Finally, please go over these safety rules while we get the prisoner ready. You'll be taken to the visiting room once everything is set up.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Phew...

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Finally.
Five minutes.
Ten minutes.
Twenty minutes.
The tea is now cold, and time seems to slow down during the wait for the jailer to return.

steps.name: Jailer
steps.text: Everything's ready. Please sign the safety rules, and I'll take you to the visiting room.

steps.name: Bibeak
steps.text: Alright, thank you.

steps.name: Prisoner
steps.text: ...You're here, kind lady!

steps.name: Prisoner
steps.text: You read my letter, didn't you? You listened to me and decided to give yourself a chance for us to put the past to rest and find peace!

steps.name: Prisoner
steps.text: The doctor was right. I should forgive myself and let my issues go. I found peace, and so can you!

steps.name: Prisoner
steps.text: Thank you so much, kind lady!
Bibeak silently hands over a package.

steps.name: Prisoner
steps.text: Is this for me?

steps.name: Prisoner
steps.text: ...What's this? A letter... my letter to you? Why did you bring it back?
He extends his hands in excitement, trying to squeeze them through the window's gaps to touch Bibeak's trembling hands.
His gaze meets hers.
She opens her mouth and utters a single phrase.
Then she stands up, turns around, and leaves the visiting room.
She hears the sound of the prisoner banging on the glass, and sees the guards rush into the room. The sounds fade away until she no longer hears them, nor does she care to.
Bibeak heads through the long hallway and goes outside.
It is a beautiful day. She looks at the clear skies and exhales.
